# Boston Celtics 2026/27 Season Outlook - No Jaylen Brown, Still A Contender?

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-07-30, 40:08. https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8

## Summary

Josh Lloyd talks with John Karalis of Locked On Celtics about the Boston Celtics after the Jaylen Brown for Paul George trade. They think the roster is better than at the start of last regular season because Jayson Tatum is back, but Karalis predicts 48 wins because the East is stronger and late-season tanking will drop off. Karalis's projected starters are Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Tatum, George and Mitchell Robinson, with Payton Pritchard as sixth man. Both reject the idea of a Brunson-style breakout for Pritchard and expect his role to shrink a little. Karalis has no worries about Tatum's health, expects Derrick White's shooting to bounce back, and sees the center minutes split roughly evenly between Robinson and Neemias Queta.

## Rules and methods

- [13:03](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=783) Before expecting a breakout, check the usage picture. When more high-usage stars are on the roster, there are fewer chances for role players, not more.
  > "the whole usage calculation is actually more crowded because you've got Tatum and George versus Brown"
- [13:57](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=837) Age matters for breakout talk. A player who has been in the league a long time and is turning 29 is probably who he is, not someone due for a breakout.
  > "He's going to be 29. He kind of is who he is."
- [17:10](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030) A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When stars return, expect some step back rather than growth.
  > "That That was last season. I would expect somewhat of a ramp backwards."
- [25:24](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1524) After major lower-body surgery, soreness on the other side from compensating is common. It does not by itself make a player injury-prone.
  > "people can question whether that injury is now is injury-prone. Like that's just a really common impact"
- [36:54](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=2214) Late-season games in March and April are skewed by teams tanking. Fewer tanking teams this season means good teams win fewer games and bad teams win more.
  > "whatever happens in March and April is basically fake. You know, 80% of the games"
- [29:50](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1790) Starting a poor free throw shooter can protect him from hack-a-player tactics, because there are no team fouls early in the game.
  > "there are no team fouls at the beginning of a game and you can't play the hack-a-Mitch"
